title: Siltvelt’s Carriage
paragraphs: We skipped breakfast, and Father made us a bento using the leftovers from yesterday. When we arrived at the riverside, Yuki-chan and the others came to greet us.
“You’ve grown even bigger again.”
“Gua!”
“You’re still making that cracking sound… Is that really okay?”
“No problem at all.”
“Guaaa.”
Sakura-chan affectionately rubbed against Father.
“Alright, let’s head out. We’ll be leveling up until evening today.”
“Yeah. Naofumi, send Sakura over here.”
“Wait a moment. I’ll be the one riding Sakura-san.”

Ren and Itsuki started glaring at each other. Sakura-chan sure is popular. By the way, they’ve both taken the powerful anti-motion sickness medicine I made, so they should be fine for a while. It’s a pity they can’t enjoy the true comfort of riding a Filolial.
“What about you, Eclair-san?”
“Me? As I mentioned yesterday, I’ll be guarding Iwatani-dono.”
“Sounds good to me.”
Ren and Itsuki decided to settle the matter of who would ride Sakura-chan with a game of rock-paper-scissors. However… they kept tying.
“Itsuki, stop changing your play from scissors to something else!”
He was switching between a normal peace-sign scissors and a different version sometimes called “country scissors,” where the fingers are shaped like a gun.
“You’re one to talk, Ren-san! Stop faking out by switching from rock to paper, then to scissors!”
“I’ve never seen such an intense game of rock-paper-scissors before.”

And honestly, their tricks were pretty cheap. Father looked at them, half exasperated. It was about to turn into a best-of-three match or a discussion on delayed reactions. Having no choice, Father picked some grass and turned it into a lottery draw to decide. The winner was Itsuki.
“Alright, then we’ll ride on Kou.”
“Since it’s the two of us, let’s take the cart.”
“We’ll have to be careful not to get thrown off.”
Father and Éclair had Kou pull a cart and climbed in.
“Damn… If only I had picked right that time…”
Ren, looking a bit frustrated, climbed onto Yuki-chan’s back. Did he really dislike riding a lady’s back that much? Yuki-chan, on the other hand, had a completely composed expression.
“Alright, Sakura-san, run just like you did when you carried Naofumi-san yesterday.”
Itsuki looked like he was having a great time. And Sakura-chan looked cool and confident.
“No, that’s not it. At this rate, it should be happening soon, so look forward to tonight.”
“Got it. Alright, let’s head out.”
Father turned to ask Ren and Itsuki. The two of them nodded.
“Whoa!”
“Whoa—”
“Whoa! It’s shaking, it’s shaking!”
“Go!”

I watched them as they departed. I’m looking forward to seeing how much stronger they’ll be when they return today. With that thought, I headed toward the castle town of Siltvelt. Not much has changed from last time. Using my memory as a guide, I purchased some equipment and left it in our inn room.
Should I rent another room while I’m at it? With that in mind, I stopped by a place in town that sells carriages. I didn’t visit here last time, but it’s a workshop that deals in carriages.
I quickly noticed that Siltvelt’s carriages had a slightly different design compared to Melromarc’s. They were either elaborately decorated or extremely rugged—very little in between.
Oh? There’s even a unique one assembled from monster bones. I wonder what kind of design Yuki-chan and the others would prefer.

Would they like a standard covered wagon like before? Noble carriages, the kind Fiancée often uses, are great for transportation but not very practical for traveling. A wooden one would probably be the best choice for usability. With proper maintenance, it would last a long time.

…Come to think of it, Filo-tan used a metal carriage. That high-end model with Air Wake processing, a one-of-a-kind piece that Father specially arranged for Filo-tan. I wonder if she truly loved that carriage.
Maybe I should make it my goal to create something that rivals it?
“I have money.”

I pulled out gold coins confiscated from a dragon and showed them to the carriage shop’s clerk. If he even thinks about pocketing them, he’ll get a taste of my Paralysis Lance. The clerk eyed me warily before finally accepting the gold.
“…Fine. Take it and go.”
“The change.”
When I reached out my hand, the clerk tried to nonchalantly slip the extra coins into his pocket. I swiftly thrust my spear at his throat.
“Try anything funny, and I’ll finish you off.”
“W-What the…?”
“By the way, killing a mere shopkeeper in this country wouldn’t even be a challenge, so calling the guards is pointless.”
Given the discrimination in this place, the soldiers might just attack me without question. Realizing the killing intent in my gaze, the clerk paled and returned the gold.
“I told you I was buying it, not taking it for free.”
I moved the spear just a bit closer. The tip pricked his skin.
“Eek!”
It seems my intimidation worked. Terrified, the clerk reluctantly handed over the correct change.
“I’ll be taking my leave, then.”
I took the carriage and left.
“W-What the hell was that…?”
I heard the clerk mutter as I walked away. I am the Spear Hero. I have my reasons for not revealing my identity, though.

Now then… should I head to Siltvelt’s Adventurer’s Guild to gather information? As I approached the guild, I noticed the demi-humans whispering among themselves. It seems rumors about the Shield Hero being summoned in Melromarc were spreading non-stop. Unfortunately, I can’t read Siltvelt’s written language. I have no idea what kind of quests are posted.
Oh? There’s an article written in a script used in Melromarc as well. The headline states that the heroes went missing after being summoned. As for the details…
It says that the heroes realized Melromarc’s conspiracy and suddenly vanished from the country. However, there’s no mention of anything about the deaths of Trash or Bitch.
“How strange.”
Considering that Trash got what he deserved, you’d think it would make the news.

Ah, I see! Even if Trash dies, it’s not newsworthy! This is a major discovery! Oh, there’s another article about the Three Heroes Church, stating that divine punishment was dealt to them. It mentions that the church was burned down by the heroes.

Did they take care of the Pope? Since I didn’t feel any resistance back then, I should check later to make sure. For now, the priority is making sure Father and the others can defend themselves against attackers. I’ll be staying in Siltvelt for a while. With that thought, I left the guild, pulling the carriage along. Then, just as I entered an alley— A group of rough-looking demi-humans and beastmen surrounded me from both the front and back.
“You got the better of me yesterday, but now I’ve brought some friends! Hand over anything valuable!”
